# Tom Butler

> Full Stack AI Engineer in York, UK. I set up private, local AI systems for businesses: open models running on their own hardware, private RAG over their own documents, and honest audits of what AI is actually costing them. The theme of everything: AI you own, not AI you rent.

Contact: dev@thomasjbutler.me

## Services

- [Services](https://thomasjbutler.github.io/services): Local & Private AI (Ollama and open-model LLM setups, private RAG knowledge systems, AI cost and privacy audits), plus web apps, backend and APIs, AI automation, mobile applications, design, and consultancy. Includes fixed-fee pricing (AI Cost & Privacy Audit from £6,000; Local LLM Setup from £12,000; Private RAG System from £18,000; Care & Tuning retainer from £1,400/month), the revision and iteration policy, and an FAQ covering hardware, GDPR, exactly what does and does not leave the machine, how the setup is hardened, and when NOT to move to local AI.

## Privacy, stated precisely

Your data never leaves the machine. The model itself arrives via a one-off download from a registry, at a time you choose, before any of your documents are near it. After that there is no API call, no per-query egress, and no third-party processor to assess. Hardening is part of the setup: the Ollama API is bound to localhost and put behind auth rather than left listening on 0.0.0.0, automatic update checks are disabled, and models are pre-pulled, so the machine can be genuinely air-gapped if it needs to be.

## Work

- [Case study](https://thomasjbutler.github.io/case-study): ISQ Agent, a RAG agent that drafts supplier security questionnaires, grounds every answer in the customer's own policy documents with citations, scores confidence on each answer, and routes weak ones to a human. Python/FastAPI RAG engine with an n8n orchestration tier, 480+ tests. The showcase build ran on hosted models (Claude, Voyage, Pinecone); the model sits behind an interface, so the same pipeline runs against open models on the customer's own hardware.
- [Projects](https://thomasjbutler.github.io/projects): AI, web, mobile and creative projects, including ModelViz (multi-provider AI model comparison), SQL Ball (natural language to SQL over football data), Morpheus (document Q&A with RAG), ReviewBot Protocol (automated PR review), and Sanctuary (an offline, on-device iOS app for neurodiverse users).
- [Dev Journey](https://thomasjbutler.github.io/updates): a timeline of the work, from first HTML to production AI systems.
